title: Hot, warm, cold
sub: The second film of Data that moves, in Modern data basics: in 1850, Paul Julius Reuter flies stock prices by pigeon across the gap between two telegraph lines, so they arrive before his clients must act; at the university, how fresh each kind of data must be is set by when someone acts on it: each faculty's spending worked out every night, contract changes every five minutes until the new ERP joins two systems, and a bank account change checked within a second.
howto: The film is drawn as the platform map up close: a dark navy night with lanes of light. Light blue is data moving and the platform, gold what people agree, green a check that passes, amber a person's turn, lilac with a lock what is personal. Temperature is how soon data must arrive for the action it serves, shown by how it moves: hot data at the top, each event the moment it happens; warm data in the middle, in small batches every few minutes; cold data at the foot, once a night, still between its runs. The tools' pages are drawn for the film.
